draft.title: Dispersion, rainbows and mirages
card: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its colours. It happens because a material has a slightly different refractive index for each colour.
In glass, violet light slows more than red light, so violet bends more. A prism shows this as a band of colours from red to violet.
In a rainbow, light refracts as it enters a raindrop, reflects off the back inside the drop, then refracts again as it leaves. Each colour leaves at a slightly different angle.
A mirage forms when air near the ground is much warmer than the air above. The refractive index changes with height, so light bends gradually and can seem to come from a pool of water.
draft.remember: Colours bend by different amounts. Warm air also bends light.

a.q: Why does a glass prism split white light into colours?
opts: Each colour has a different refractive index in glass
Each colour travels at a different speed in a vacuum
The prism adds colour to the light as it passes
Red light reflects off the prism and violet light does not
a.why: Each colour has a slightly different refractive index in glass, so each bends by a different amount. In a vacuum all colours travel at the same speed c, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about how much each colour bends at the surface.

b.q: On a hot day, Sam sees a shimmering patch that looks like water on a highway ahead. What causes it?
opts: Light bends in the warm air just above the road
Light reflects off a thin layer of real water
Raindrops split the light into its colours
The road surface gives out its own blue light
b.why: Air just above the hot road has a different refractive index from the cooler air above it, so light bends and seems to come from the ground. Raindrops cause rainbows, not mirages.
b.clue: Think about what is different about the air near the road.

a.best: Each colour has a different refractive index in glass

b.best: Light bends in the warm air just above the road
